# In-place truncate is safe throughout: mangosd holds these logs
# O_APPEND, so it keeps writing from offset 0 (no orphaned handle,
# no restart). Plain truncate (not cp) on the cores-dir logs so it
# can never wedge on a full disk the way a cp would.
ACTIVE_CAP_KB=$((2 * 1024 * 1024))   # rotate active Server log past 2 GiB
CAP_KB=$((12 * 1024 * 1024))         # keep ~12 GiB of Server-log history
LOG_CAP_KB=$((1024 * 1024))          # 1 GiB per cores-dir log
prune() {
  while true; do
    # /opt/mangos/cores: keep 2 newest non-zero core dumps, and
    # cap the relative-path logs mangosd writes here (it cd's here
    # for core capture): DBErrors.log, Char.log, EventAIErrors.log,
    # SD2Errors.log — DBErrors.log hit 11G on live / filled PTR.
    if cd /opt/mangos/cores 2>/dev/null; then
      find . -maxdepth 1 -name 'core.*' -size 0 -delete 2>/dev/null
      # shellcheck disable=SC2012
      ls -1t core.* 2>/dev/null | tail -n +3 | xargs -r rm -f --
      for lf in DBErrors.log Char.log EventAIErrors.log SD2Errors.log; do
        [ -f "$lf" ] || continue
        sz=$(du -k "$lf" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
        [ -n "$sz" ] && [ "$sz" -gt "$LOG_CAP_KB" ] && : > "$lf"
      done
    fi
    # /opt/mangos/logs: copytruncate the active Server log past
    # ACTIVE_CAP_KB, drop stale 0-byte logs, budget rotated to CAP_KB.
    if cd /opt/mangos/logs 2>/dev/null; then
      # shellcheck disable=SC2012
      active=$(ls -1 Server_*.log 2>/dev/null | sort | tail -1)
      if [ -n "$active" ]; then
        sz=$(du -k "$active" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
        if [ -n "$sz" ] && [ "$sz" -gt "$ACTIVE_CAP_KB" ]; then
          secs=$(date -u +%s 2>/dev/null || echo rot)
          # NB: destination uses the no-brace var form on purpose. The
          # brace form is eaten by Flux post-build substitution (undefined
          # vars become empty, collapsing the path to a bare dot -> cp
          # fails same-file), which silently broke this copytruncate.
          cp "$active" "$active.$secs" 2>/dev/null && : > "$active"
        fi
      fi
      find . -maxdepth 1 -name '*.log' -size 0 -mmin +5 -delete 2>/dev/null
      total=0
      # shellcheck disable=SC2012
      ls -1t Server_*.log* 2>/dev/null | grep -vxF "$active" | while read -r f; do
        sz=$(du -k "$f" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)
        [ -n "$sz" ] || continue
        total=$((total + sz))
        [ "$total" -gt "$CAP_KB" ] && rm -f -- "$f"
      done
    fi
    sleep 600
  done
}
prune &

until nc -z cmangos-database 3306; do sleep 2; done

set -u
# /bin/bash because the mariadb:12.2 image is Ubuntu-
# based with no `nc` and /bin/sh = dash (no /dev/tcp).
# bash's pseudo-device probes the TCP port with no
# external tools — small, fast, and survives image
# rebuilds without extra packages.
probe() {
  timeout 2 bash -c "</dev/tcp/$$1/$$2" >/dev/null 2>&1
}
# Hysteresis: flip OFFLINE on the first failed probe
# (fast "down" signal so clients stop being lured into
# clicking a half-dead realm), but require N consecutive
# successful probes before clearing OFFLINE. Prevents
# bait-and-switch during a crash loop where mangosd's
# port is briefly open between SIGSEGVs.
STABLE_REQUIRED=3
ok1=0
ok2=0
while true; do
  # Emberstone (realm id=1) ← cmangos-world:8085
  if probe cmangos-world 8085; then
    ok1=$$((ok1 + 1))
    if [ "$$ok1" -ge "$$STABLE_REQUIRED" ]; then op1="& ~2"; else op1="| 2"; fi
  else
    ok1=0; op1="| 2"
  fi
  # Emberstone PTR (realm id=2) ← cmangos-ptr-world:8086
  if probe cmangos-ptr-world 8086; then
    ok2=$$((ok2 + 1))
    if [ "$$ok2" -ge "$$STABLE_REQUIRED" ]; then op2="& ~2"; else op2="| 2"; fi
  else
    ok2=0; op2="| 2"
  fi
  mariadb -h cmangos-database -P 3306 \
    -u "$${MANGOS_DBUSER}" -p"$${MANGOS_DBPASS}" classicrealmd \
    -e "UPDATE realmlist SET realmflags = realmflags $${op1} WHERE id = 1; \
        UPDATE realmlist SET realmflags = realmflags $${op2} WHERE id = 2" \
    >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  sleep 3
done

RealmServerPort = 3724
BindIP = "0.0.0.0"
# Refresh in-memory realmlist from DB every 5s (default 20s).
# The realmflags-prober sidecar writes the OFFLINE bit
# within ~3s of a world crash; pair that with a 5s realmd
# cache so the WoW client sees the realm flip to Offline
# in <10s end-to-end instead of up to ~30s with defaults.
# Critical for the "mangosd crashed, let me pick another
# realm" UX — otherwise the launcher shows the dead realm
# as online and clicking it hangs the connect.
RealmsStateUpdateDelay = 5
# Brute-force protection on the SRP6 auth port (internet
# exposed via TCPRoute → envoy-external gateway).
#   MaxCount=5  failures before action
#   BanTime=600 ten-minute ban
#   BanType=1   ban by IP (0 = ban the account, riskier)
#   Logging=1   log every failure so Crowdsec / Falco can
#               pick up patterns and broaden the response
WrongPass.MaxCount = 5
WrongPass.BanTime = 600
WrongPass.BanType = 1
WrongPass.Logging = 1
